rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated examples answer the wealthy Meccan disbelievers' boast and expose their claim as false, yet they persist in futile disputation; taṣrīf signals repetition.
rows.anchor: التصريف يقتضي التكرير والأمر كذلك لأنه تعالى أجاب عن شبهتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا, جدلا is a tamyīz distinguishing the human as the most argumentative of things capable of disputation.
rows.anchor: وانتصاب قوله جدلا على التمييز

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: The verse implies that prophets debated religion with opponents, since disputation necessarily has two sides; this also refutes reliance on imitation alone.
rows.anchor: قال بعض المحققين والآية دالة على أن الأنبياء عليهم السلام جادلوهم في الدين

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The verse says no impediment prevented belief when guidance arrived, which they take to refute the claim that God created an impediment to belief.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : الآية دالة على أنه لم يوجد ما يمنع

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: The knowledge that a person will not believe conflicts with belief, and the motive toward disbelief also prevents belief; voluntary action cannot occur without a motive.
rows.anchor: قال أصحابنا : العلم بأنه لا يؤمن مضاد لوجود الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that nothing prevented belief concerns perceptible impediments: guidance and evidence came, excuses disappeared, and nothing outwardly blocked belief or repentance.
rows.anchor: المعنى أنه لما جاءهم الهدى وهو الدليل الدال على صحة الإسلام

rows.speaker: حمزة وعاصم والكسائي
rows.claim: They read قبلا with both ق and ب rounded, taking it as a plural of قبيل: successive kinds of punishment while the people remain alive; it may also mean face to face.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة وعاصم والكسائي قبلا بضم القاف والباء جميعا

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: They read قبلا with kasra on ق and fatḥa on ب, meaning punishment seen face to face.
rows.anchor: والباقون قبلا بكسر القاف وفتح الباء أي عيانا أيضا

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: He transmits a reading with both vowels open, interpreting قبلا as something imminent or forthcoming.
rows.anchor: وروى صاحب الكشاف قبلا بفتحتين أي مستقبلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers act as though they will believe only after exterminating punishment or successive worldly torments arrive, conditions no sensible person would accept.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أنهم لا يقدمون على الإيمان إلا عند نزول عذاب الاستئصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers bring good news of reward for obedience and warning of punishment for disobedience so people may believe willingly; disbelievers instead dispute falsely to erase truth.
rows.anchor: إنما أرسل الرسل مبشرين بالثواب على الطاعة ومنذرين بالعقاب على المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse again shows prophets debated with them, because disputation occurs between opposing parties; their mockery targets the Quran and prophetic warnings and displays ignorance and hardness.
rows.anchor: يوجد من الكفار المجادلة بالباطل لغرض دحض الحق

rows.speaker: النحويون
rows.claim: In وما أنذروا, ما may be a relative pronoun with its resumptive omitted, or a verbal noun meaning their warning.
rows.anchor: قال النحويون ما في قوله : { وما أنذروا } يجوز أن تكون موصولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one is more unjust than the disbeliever who receives clear signs and turns away; forgetting what his hands sent ahead means neglecting reflection and feigning disregard of past evil deeds and false doctrines.
rows.anchor: لا ظلم أعظم من كفر من ترد عليه الآيات والبينات فيعرض عنها

rows.speaker: القدرية
rows.claim: They cite the warning and turning away as evidence for human agency and responsibility.
rows.anchor: قوله : { ومن أظلم ممن ذكر بئايات ربه فأعرض عنها ونسى ما قدمت يداه } متمسك القدرية

rows.speaker: الجبرية
rows.claim: They cite God placing coverings on hearts and deafness in ears as evidence for determinism; the Quran often pairs a verse for each opposing school.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { إنا جعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة أن يفقهوه } إلى آخر الآية متمسك الجبرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired verses are a severe divine test that distinguishes firmly grounded scholars from imitators, and experience confirms the pattern.
rows.anchor: وما ذاك إلا امتحان شديد من الله تعالى ألقاه على عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ghafūr emphasizes withholding harm, while mercy is named without an intensifier: God has withheld limitless harms despite power to inflict them, whereas acts of mercy are finite.
rows.anchor: لأن المغفرة ترك الإضرار وهو تعالى قد ترك مضار لا نهاية لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative is that God forgives abundantly because He is merciful and gives mercy freely to many needy recipients.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يقال : المراد أنه يغفر كثيرا لأنه ذو الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deferred موعد may be the Resurrection or a worldly date such as Badr and the other days of conquest; موئل means refuge or shelter, from وءل, to seek refuge.
rows.anchor: وهو إما يوم القيامة ، وإما في الدنيا وهو يوم بدر وسائر أيام الفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The villages are those of earlier peoples such as Thamud and Lot, offered as a lesson; they were destroyed for wrongdoing like Mecca's people, at a fixed appointed time.
rows.anchor: يريد قرى الأولين من ثمود وقوم لوط وغيرهم أشار إليها ليعتبروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, وتلك begins the clause, القرى describes the demonstrative by a genus, and أهلكناهم is its predicate, meaning the people of those towns were destroyed.
rows.anchor: وتلك مبتدأ ، والقرى صفة لأن أسماء الإشارة توصف بأصناف الأجناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading لمهلكهم has an open mīm and either open or kasra lām, meaning their destruction or its time; موعد can mean time or verbal noun, and the set term brings them nearer repentance.
rows.anchor: وقرىء لمهلكهم بفتح الميم واللام مفتوحة أو مكسورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story of Moses seeking knowledge from Khidr is independent, but serves both prior narratives: it teaches humility over pride and answers the Jews' test of Muhammad by showing prophethood does not entail knowing every story.
rows.anchor: موسى عليه السلام مع كثرة علمه وعمله وعلو منصبه واستجماع موجبات الشرف التام

rows.speaker: أكثر العلماء
rows.claim: Most scholars identify this Moses as Moses son of Amram, possessor of the Torah and manifest miracles.
rows.anchor: أكثر العلماء على أن موسى المذكور في هذه الآية هو موسى بن عمران

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr tells Ibn ʿAbbās that Nawf, son of Kaʿb's wife, claimed Khidr's companion was Moses son of Misha son of Joseph, not Moses son of Amram; Ibn ʿAbbās calls the claim a lie.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير أنه قال لابن عباس : إن نوفا ابن امرأة كعب يزعم أن الخضر ليس صاحب

rows.speaker: جمهور اليهود
rows.claim: The majority Jewish account identifies the seeker as Moses son of Misha, who sought knowledge from Khidr and accompanied him in the ship, the killing, and the wall episode.
rows.anchor: هذا هو قول جمهور اليهود

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal argues that an unqualified Quranic reference to Moses means the famous Torah-bearing prophet; a different Moses would need a distinguishing description, as with the familiar name Abu Hanifa.
rows.anchor: قال إن الله تعالى ما ذكر موسى في كتابه إلا وأراد به صاحب التوراة

rows.speaker: مخالفو القفال
rows.claim: They argue it is unlikely that Moses was sent to learn after receiving the Torah, direct speech from God, and extraordinary miracles; the response is that even a great scholar may need to learn some matters from someone below him.
rows.anchor: وحجة الذين قالوا : موسى هذا غير صاحب التوراة أنه تعالى بعد أن أنزل التوراة عليه

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most commentators identify Moses' young companion as Joshua son of Nun.
rows.anchor: فالأكثرون على أنه يوشع بن نون

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report transmitted by al-Qaffal through Ubayy ibn Kaʿb identifies Moses' young companion as Joshua son of Nun.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول فتاه يوشع بن نون

rows.speaker: القول الثاني
rows.claim: A second view says the companion was Joshua's brother, who accompanied Moses on this journey.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : أن فتى موسى أخو يوشع وكان صاحبا لموسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, in a report from ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd, interprets فتاه as Moses' servant; al-Qaffal says Arabic usage supports this because slaves were called young man or young woman.
rows.anchor: والقول الثالث : روى عمرو بن عبيد عن الحسن في قوله : { وإذ قال موسى لفتاه لا أبرح } قال يعني عبده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says that after receiving the tablets Moses asked who was more excellent and knowledgeable, and was told of Khidr, a servant dwelling on the sea islands.
rows.anchor: قيل إن موسى عليه السلام لما أعطي الألواح وكلمه الله تعالى قال : من الذي أفضل مني وأعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Moses thought no one surpassed his knowledge; Gabriel used a bird taking a beakful from the sea to illustrate how little creaturely knowledge is beside God's.
rows.anchor: يهوي إلى البحر يضرب بمنقاره فيه ثم يرتفع فأنت فيما أوتيت من العلم

rows.speaker: الأصوليون
rows.claim: The theologians call that report weak: prophets know God's knowledge is unbounded while created knowledge is finite and always can be exceeded, so Moses could not reasonably think no one knew more.
rows.anchor: قال الأصوليون : هذه الرواية ضعيفة لأن الأنبياء يجب أن يعلموا أن معلومات الله لا نهاية لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third account says God names the most beloved servant as one who remembers Him, the most just as one who judges by truth, and the most learned as one who seeks others' knowledge; God directs Moses to Khidr by the fish sign.
rows.anchor: قال : فأي عبادك أعلم ؟ قال : الذي يبتغي علم الناس إلى علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this account the fish revives and jumps into the sea while Moses sleeps; Khidr then explains that their knowledge compared with God's is like a bird's sip compared with the ocean.
rows.anchor: ما ينقص علمي وعلمك من علم الله مقدار ما أخذ هذا العصفور من البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bird's finite sip relative to a finite sea differs from all created knowledge, finite, relative to God's unlimited knowledge; the two ratios are not comparable.
rows.anchor: نسبة معلومات جميع المخلوقات إلى معلومات الله تعالى نسبة متناه إلى غير متناه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says لا أبرح cannot mean I do not move, since Moses did travel; al-Razi answers that departing from something can mean abandoning it, so the phrase means not ceasing the journey.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج قوله : { لا أبرح } ليس معناه لا أزول ، لأنه لو كان كذلك لم يقطع أرضا

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most take لا أبرح as لا أزال; Arabs also use لا أزال, لا أنفك, and لا أفتأ for continued persistence in an action.
rows.anchor: المشهور عند الجمهور أن قوله لا أبرح معناه لا أزول

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal derives لا أبرح from البراح, absence: denying absence means remaining, so the phrase expresses persistence; its predicate is omitted because the travel context and حتى clause supply it.
rows.anchor: فقوله لا أبرح يكون عدما للعدم فيكون ثبوتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted predicate can mean I will keep travelling until the meeting point, or I will not leave my present pursuit until I reach it.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون المعنى لا أبرح مما أنا عليه يعني ألزم المسير والطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meeting place was promised as Khidr's location; it is often said to be where the Persian and Roman seas meet in the east, but the verse does not identify the seas, so one should remain silent absent a sound report; another metaphor calls Moses and Khidr seas of knowledge.
rows.anchor: وليس في اللفظ ما يدل على تعيين هذين البحرين فإن صح بالخبر الصحيح شيء فذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading مجمع with kasra on mīm is reported; حقبا means a long time, with some defining it as eighty years, and the same word is discussed at 78:23.
rows.anchor: وقرىء مجمع بكسر الميم ثم قال أو أمضي حقبا أي أسير زمانا طويلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses had been told the learned servant's qualities but not his exact location, so he vowed to endure a long, difficult journey to seek knowledge; a student may travel from east to west for one question.
rows.anchor: وهذا إخبار من موسى بأنه وطن نفسه على تحمل التعب الشديد والعناء العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For مجمع بينهما, one view takes it as the meeting of the two seas, fulfilling Moses' words; another takes it as the place where Moses and Khidr meet, near Khidr's home, which explains their return there; commentators prefer the first.
rows.anchor: والمفسرون على القول الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fish's revival was the sign identifying Khidr's particular dwelling: either the sign itself indicated that place or Moses was to follow the fish's route.
rows.anchor: فيحتمل أنه قيل له فهنالك موضعه ويحتمل أنه قيل له فاذهب على موافقة ذهاب ذلك الحوت

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One report says the young companion was washing the salted fish when it jumped away.
rows.anchor: قيل إن الفتى كان يغسل السمكة لأنها كانت مملحة فطفرت وسارت

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says Joshua performed ablution there, splashing water onto the salted fish, which revived and leapt into the water.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن يوشع توضأ في ذلك المكان فانتضح الماء على الحوت المالح

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third report says a spring from Paradise burst forth and drops reached the fish, reviving it so it leapt into the sea.
rows.anchor: وقيل انفجر ( ت ) هناك عين من الجنة ووصلت قطرات من تلك العين إلى السمكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their forgetting the fish means they forgot how this unusual event signified arrival at the goal; Joshua may have forgotten because he had seen many great miracles from Moses.
rows.anchor: المراد من قوله : { نسيا حوتهما } أنهما نسيا كيفية الاستدلال بهذه الحالة المخصوصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi also proposes that God removed this necessary knowledge from Joshua's heart to teach Moses that knowledge depends on God's instruction and preservation.
rows.anchor: أزال الله عن قلب صاحبه هذا العلم الضروري تنبيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing of سربا supplies an omitted verb, as if the fish ساربا ساربا; another treats اتخذ as standing in for سار, with سرب meaning going, as in 13:10.
rows.anchor: والسرب هو الذهاب ومنه قوله : { وسارب بالنهار }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God held back the sea's water and made a vaulted passage for the fish; after they passed the sign and travelled on, hunger and fatigue made Moses ask for breakfast.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى أمسك إجراء الماء على البحر وجعله كالطاق والكوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In أرأيت, the hamza is interrogative and رأيت retains its literal sense; idiomatically one asks this when reporting something astonishing, with its object supplied by the next clause.
rows.anchor: الهمزة في أرأيت همزة الاستفهام ورأيت على معناه الأصلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about Satan intervenes between coordinated clauses as an excuse explaining the lapse: I forgot the fish, and it took its way into the sea.
rows.anchor: أنه اعتراض وقع بين المعطوف والمعطوف عليه والتقدير فإني نسيت الحوت

rows.speaker: الكعبي
rows.claim: Al-Kaʿbi says attributing the forgetfulness to Satan means God neither created nor willed it; otherwise it should be attributed to God and Satan would have no effect.
rows.anchor: قال الكعبي : { وما أنسانيه إلا الشيطان أن أذكره } يدل على أنه تعالى ما خلق ذلك النسيان

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The judge explains Satan's role as occupying the heart with his whisperings, not memory loss that opposes recall, which can only come from God.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالنسيان أن يشتغل قلب الإنسان بوساوسه التي هي من فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase أن أذكره is an appositive replacement for the pronoun in أنسانيه, meaning the fish's mention or remembrance.
rows.anchor: قوله : أن اذكره بدل من الهاء في أنسانيه أي : وما أنساني ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عجبا may modify an omitted verbal noun, because the fish revived, left the basket, and leapt away unseen; or it may describe God's tunnel through the water; alternatively it is a separate exclamation by Moses or the narrator.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد منه ما ذكرنا أنه تعالى جعل الماء عليه كالطاق وكالسرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says this is what they sought because the fish was the sign of finding Khidr; نبغ drops its final yā for ease, unusually for a verb, by analogy with its deletion before a following consonant.
rows.anchor: قال موسى ذلك الذي كنا نطلبه لأنه أمارة الظفر بالمطلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قصصا can be a circumstantial verbal noun, meaning they returned tracing their tracks, or an absolute verbal noun for فارتدا because that means they followed their tracks.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { قصصا } فيه وجهان : أحدهما : أنه مصدر في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once they realized they had passed the learned man's dwelling, they retraced their route to it.
rows.anchor: لما عرفا أنهما تجاوزا عن الموضع الذي يسكن فيه ذلك العالم رجعا

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most scholars say the servant was a prophet. Their first proof is that mercy from God means prophethood, supported by 43:32 and 28:86; the response is that prophethood is mercy but not every mercy is prophethood.
rows.anchor: قال الأكثرون إن ذلك العبد كان نبيا واحتجوا عليه بوجوه

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Their second proof is that God taught him directly without a human teacher, which they regard as prophetic revelation; al-Razi replies that necessary knowledge also comes directly from God without proving prophethood.
rows.anchor: وهذا يقتضي أنه تعالى علمه لا بواسطة تعليم معلم ولا إرشاد مرشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi rejects the proof that Moses' request to follow Khidr makes Khidr a prophet: the restriction on prophetic learning does not extend to all other knowledge.
rows.anchor: والنبي لا يتبع غير النبي / في التعليم وهذا أيضا ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi rejects the proof that Khidr's apparent superiority and Moses' humility make Khidr a prophet: a nonprophet may surpass a prophet in fields unrelated to prophethood.
rows.anchor: الحجة الرابعة : أن ذلك العبد أظهر الترفع على موسى حيث قال له : { صبرا وكيف تصبر على ما لم تحط به خبرا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that such a teacher-student relation deters people fails: if Moses' post-Torah learning from Khidr does not deter, the alleged difficulty here does not either.
rows.anchor: قلنا فارسال موسى إلى التعلم منه بعد إنزال الله عليه التوراة وتكليمه بغير واسطة يوجب التنفير

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm takes وما فعلته عن أمري to mean Khidr acted by God's revelation, evidence that he was a prophet; al-Razi calls the argument plainly weak.
rows.anchor: الحجة الخامسة : احتج الأصم على نبوته بقوله في أثناء القصة : { وما فعلته عن أمرى } ومعناه فعلته بوحي الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Khidr greeted Moses as Prophet of the Israelites; when asked who told him, he said the one who sent Moses, implying revelation and prophethood, though al-Razi allows it could be a wonder or inspiration.
rows.anchor: قال : الذي بعثك إلي . قالوا وهذا يدل على أنه إنما عرف ذلك بالوحي والوحي لا يكون إلا مع النبوة

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most identify the servant as Khidr; he was so named because any place where he stood became green.
rows.anchor: إنما سمي بالخضر لأنه كان لا يقف موقفا إلا أخضر ذلك الموضع

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says reports place Khidr's commissioning after Moses and make him an Israelite; if so, this servant cannot be Khidr.
rows.anchor: قال الجبائي قد ظهرت الرواية أن الخضر إنما بعث بعد موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Khidr is both this servant and a prophet, the argument that he outranks Moses creates an impossibility: an Israelite cannot outrank his prophet, while a non-Israelite cannot outrank Moses given Israel's favor; this supports another Moses.
rows.anchor: وهذه الكلمات تقوي قول من يقول : إن موسى هذا غير موسى صاحب التوراة

rows.speaker: الصوفية
rows.claim: Sufis call knowledge received through spiritual unveiling, without an intermediary, knowledge from God; al-Ghazali wrote a treatise establishing such knowledge.
rows.anchor: والصوفية سموا العلوم الحاصلة بطريق المكاشفات العلوم اللدنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi distinguishes conceptual apprehension and judgment, each either intuitive or acquired; immediate examples include pain, pleasure, existence, nonexistence, noncontradiction, and one being half of two.
rows.anchor: فإما أن نحكم عليه بحكم وهو التصديق أو لا نحكم وهو التصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Acquired knowledge comes either from combining self-evident premises through reasoning and reflection, or from ascetic discipline that weakens sense and imagination so the intellect receives divine light without deliberative effort; the latter is ladunni knowledge.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو المسمى بالعلوم اللدنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rational souls differ: the pure, luminous soul, little attached to bodily desires, receives sacred lights fully from the unseen realm; this is the ladunni knowledge meant here.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو المراد بالعلم اللدني وهو المراد من قوله : { رحمة من عندنا وعلمناه من لدنا علما قال }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A less lucid soul can acquire knowledge only through a human teacher; the contrast is like sun versus scattered lights, sea versus streams, and the supreme spirit versus partial spirits.
rows.anchor: والقسم الأول بالنسبة إلى القسم الثاني كالشمس بالنسبة إلى الأضواء الجزئية

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr and Yaʿqub read رشدا with fatḥa on both letters; Ibn ʿAbbas is reported with ḍamma on both, and the remaining readers use ḍamma on rāʾ and sukūn on shīn.
rows.anchor: المسألة الأولى : قرأ أبو عمرو ويعقوب { رشدا } بفتح الراء والشين وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما بضم الراء والشين

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal says these are dialect variants with the same meaning, and رشدا means knowledge that carries right guidance; the guidance may be Khidr's or Moses', depending on the reading of the phrase.
rows.anchor: قال القفال وهي لغات في معنى واحد

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: One interpretation makes the requested guidance Khidr's, from what God taught and guided him by; another makes it guidance for Moses through the teaching he receives.
rows.anchor: قال القفال قوله : { رشدا } يحتمل وجهين : أحدهما : أن يكون الرشد راجعا إلى الخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' request models humility: he makes himself a follower and first asks permission to follow, rather than assuming the role.
rows.anchor: فأحدها : أنه جعل نفسه تبعا له لأنه قال : { هل أتبعك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He admits his own ignorance and the teacher's knowledge, then asks only for some of what God taught Khidr, like a poor person requesting a portion from the rich.
rows.anchor: وصيغة من للتبعيض فطلب منه تعليم بعض ما علمه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By saying مما علمت, Moses acknowledges that God taught Khidr; by asking for رشدا, he seeks guidance that prevents error and straying.
rows.anchor: وخامسها : أن قوله : { مما علمت } اعتراف بأن الله علمه ذلك العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks Khidr to benefit him as God benefited Khidr; the saying that one is a servant of whoever taught a letter illustrates honoring one's teacher.
rows.anchor: ولهذا المعنى قيل أنا عبد من تعلمت منه حرفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following means doing another's act because that person did it, unlike independently repeating a shared creed; students should initially submit and avoid disputation.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن المتعلم يجب عليه في أول الأمر التسليم وترك المنازعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unqualified request to follow Khidr seeks to imitate him in every matter, without restricting the request to one kind of act.
rows.anchor: يدل على طلب متابعته مطلقا في جميع الأمور غير مقيد بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Moses knew Khidr knew he was the Torah-bearing prophet spoken to directly by God, Moses still displayed exceptional humility; deeper knowledge increases one's appreciation and pursuit of learning and respect for scholars.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه عليه السلام مع هذه المناصب الرفيعة والدرجات العالية الشريفة أتى بهذه الأنواع الكثيرة من التواضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses first offers service by proposing to follow, then asks for teaching; he seeks knowledge alone, without requesting wealth or rank.
rows.anchor: فلم يطلب على تلك المتابعة على التعليم شيئا كان قال لا أطلب منك على هذه المتابعة المال والجاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A student accustomed to argument may misread an outwardly troubling act, challenge an advanced teacher, and provoke estrangement; Khidr's warning refers to Moses' argumentative habits and lack of knowledge of hidden realities.
rows.anchor: حكى عن الخضر أنه قال : { إنك لن تستطيع معى صبرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teaching a learned disputant is especially difficult: he is practiced in debate, mistakes apparent wrong for real wrong, objects before grasping the truth, and can alienate a complete teacher after repeated clashes.
rows.anchor: فهذا المتعلم لأجل أنه ألف القيل والقال وتعود الكلام والجدال يغتر ظاهره

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: The Sunni theologians infer that capacity does not precede action: if Moses already had capacity to be patient, Khidr's statement that he could not be patient would be false.
rows.anchor: المسألة الثانية : احتج أصحابنا بقوله : { إنك لن تستطيع معى صبرا } على أن الاستطاعة لا تحصل قبل الفعل

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i interprets لن تستطيع idiomatically as patience being difficult, as when someone says he cannot bear to see another; al-Razi rejects this as an unsupported departure from the apparent sense and uses the following question to reinforce his argument.
rows.anchor: أجاب الجبائي عنه : أن المراد من هذا القول أنه يثقل عليه الصبر

rows.speaker: الطاعنون في عصمة الأنبياء
rows.claim: Critics say Khidr predicts Moses will fail to be patient while Moses promises patience if God wills, so one prophet must lie; al-Razi answers that Khidr describes the usual or predominant outcome, avoiding contradiction.
rows.anchor: والجواب أن يحمل قوله : { إنك لن تستطيع معى صبرا } على الأكثر الأغلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional إن شاء الله expresses uncertainty about whether God wills Moses' patience; since patience is obligatory, this supports the view that God may command what He does not will.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على صحة قولنا : إن الله تعالى قد يأمر بالشيء مع أنه لا يريده

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They say إن شاء الله is merely courteous wording for an intended future act; al-Razi argues that if the wording has real meaning it supports his point, and if false it is no etiquette.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : هذه الكلمة إنما تذكر رعاية للأدب فيما يريد الإنسان أن يفعله في المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' promise not to disobey indicates that the apparent force of a command is obligation: whoever disobeys God and His Messenger merits Hell.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن ظاهر الأمر يفيد الوجوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' humility and Khidr's admonition model teaching: students should be deeply humble, while teachers may speak firmly when it benefits and protects a student from pride that blocks learning.
rows.anchor: أن الواجب على المتعلم إظهار التواضع بأقصى الغايات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr tells Moses not to question an act he sees before Khidr initiates an explanation of it.
rows.anchor: أي لا تستخبرني عما تراه مني مما لا تعلم وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAmir reads the prohibition with a vocalized lām and doubled nūn without yāʾ; a report from him and Nafiʿ retains yāʾ with a heavy form, while the remaining readers use a light nūn; the meaning is the same.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن عامر فلا تسألن محركة اللام مشددة النون بغير ياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi conjectures that Khidr damaged the boat so it looked visibly defective and would not sink quickly.
rows.anchor: لعله أقدم على خرق جدار السفينة لتصير السفينة بسبب ذلك الخرق معيبة ظاهرة العيب

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read the verb with the people as subject, assigning the sinking to the boat's occupants; the other readers address Khidr, meaning you would sink its people.
rows.anchor: البحث الأول : قرأ حمزة والكسائي : { أعزة أهلها } بفتح الياء على إسناد الغرق إلى الأهل

rows.speaker: الطاعنون في عصمة الأنبياء
rows.claim: Critics argue Moses either falsely accused a prophet of a grave sin or truthfully exposed Khidr's sin, and that he broke his solemn promise not to object.
rows.anchor: واحتج الطاعنون في عصمة الأنبياء عليهم السلام بهذه الآية من وجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses spoke because the action was extraordinary and wanted to learn its reason, not because he believed Khidr had done wrong; امر may describe something astonishing.
rows.anchor: لا لأجل أنه اعتقد فيه أنه فعل قبيحا ، بل لأنه أحب أن يقف على وجهه وسببه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses broke the condition through forgetfulness, so the lapse is excused; رهق means to overwhelm, and he asks Khidr not to make the follow-up journey difficult by reproaching him, while one reading has عسرا with two ḍammas.
rows.anchor: وعلى الثاني : أنه فعل بناء على النسيان ، ثم إنه تعالى حكى عن ذلك العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غلام can mean an adolescent, as a poem contrasts an old man with a young man and its root relates to youthful sexual desire, or simply a small child; the Quran leaves his setting, faith, age, and manner of killing unspecified.
rows.anchor: وليس في القرآن كيف لقياه هل كان يلعب مع جمع من الغلمان الصبيان أو كان منفردا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the word suits a child, بغير نفس more readily suggests an adult because a child is not subject to killing; the verse gives no method of killing.
rows.anchor: إلا أن قوله : { بغير نفس } أليق بالبالغ منه بالصبي

rows.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: They read زاكية with alif; the others read زكية without it. Al-Kisai treats the forms as synonymous for purity, while Abu ʿAmr says زاكية is one who never sinned and زكية one who sinned then repented.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو زاكية بالألف والباقون زكية بغير ألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses appears to think killing is lawful only as retaliation for another life, though other grounds can make blood lawful; retaliation is simply the strongest and clearest ground.
rows.anchor: وجوابه أن السبب الأقوى هو ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi says the boy's killing is more reprehensible than puncturing the boat: the boat might not sink and no life was certainly lost, whereas the boy's death was certain; nukr may also mean what reason rejects and souls recoil from.
rows.anchor: وهذا إشارة إلى أن قتل الغلام أقبح من خرق السفينة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes امر as astonishing and nukr as stronger than astonishment; another says nukr is what reason and the soul reject, making it harsher than امر.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن قوله : { لقد جئت شيئا إمرا } أي عجبا والنكر أعظم من العجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others rank امر as more severe because a damaged boat might kill many, while the boy's death took one life, and امر means a great calamity.
rows.anchor: قال : لأن خرق السفينة يؤدي إلى إتلاف نفوس كثيرة وهذ القتل ليس إلا إتلاف شخص واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added word لك in ألم أقل لك intensifies the reproach.
rows.anchor: إلا أنه زاد ههنا لفظة لك لأن هذه اللفظة تؤكد التوبيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses deeply regrets the next breach despite strongly wanting the companionship, and praises Khidr for bearing with him twice so soon.
rows.anchor: مع العلم بشدة حرصه على مصاحبته وهذا كلام نادم شديد الندامة

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: They read نكرا with ḍamma on kāf throughout the Quran; the remaining readers leave it unvowelled, the two being dialects.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع برواية ورش وقالون وابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم نكرا بضم الكاف

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqub reads لا تصحبني without alif; all others read لا تصاحبني, with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: الثاني : الكل قرأوا : { لا * تصاحبنى } بالألف إلا يعقوب فإنه قرأ : ( لا تصحبني ) من صحب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings of لدني include light nūn with ḍamma dāl, doubled nūn with ḍamma dāl, an ishmām form without full prolongation, and ḍamma lām with sukūn dāl; all are dialect variants.
rows.anchor: وهذه القراءات كلها لغات في هذه اللفظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The village is identified as Antioch, while another view identifies it as Eilat.
rows.anchor: أن تلك القرية هي أنطاكية وقيل هي الأيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was accustomed to stating his need, as in his prayer at Midian (28:24); asking food is permissible in all laws and may be obligatory when severe hunger threatens harm.
rows.anchor: لأن موسى كان من عادته عرض الحاجة وطلب الطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated أهل in استطعما أهلها emphasizes the request; a poet's line about the crow repeats الغراب as evidence of this kind of repetition.
rows.anchor: والجواب أن التكرير قد يكون للتأكيد كقول الشاعر : ليت الغراب غداة ينعب دائما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hospitality is usually recommended but can become obligatory if a guest is so hungry that failure to feed him risks death; otherwise Moses' anger after one night without food would be disproportionate.
rows.anchor: وقد تكون من الواجبات بأن كان الضيف قد بلغ في الجوع إلى حيث لو لم يأكل لهلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that Moses could not be near death because he could still repair the wall for a fee is answered by saying his hunger was severe but not yet fatal, so he could work and ask payment.
rows.anchor: لعل ذلك الجوع كان شديدا إلا أنه ما بلغ حد الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ضيفه means he was someone's guest, literally leaning toward him, like an arrow veering from its target; أضافه or ضيفه means he lodged him and made him a guest.
rows.anchor: يقال ضافه إذا كان له ضيفا ، وحقيقته مال إليه من ضاف السهم عن الغرض

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet describes the village's people as miserly.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كانوا أهل قرية لئاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anecdote in storybooks says the villagers, ashamed after hearing the verse, offered the Prophet gold to change one letter so it would say they came to host the travelers; he refused because altering the Quran would insert a lie and impugn divinity.
rows.anchor: رأيت في كتب الحكايات أن أهل تلك القرية لما سمعوا نزول هذه الآية استحيوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wall's desire to collapse is metaphorical because walls are not living; a poet's spear and al-Farra's personified time show this figurative usage.
rows.anchor: مع أن الإرادة من صفات الأحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran likewise predicates silence of anger, says Be and it is, and has heaven and earth say they came willingly, using nonliteral speech for nonliving things.
rows.anchor: ونظيره من القرآن قوله تعالى : { ولما سكت عن موسى الغضب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: انقض can mean it fell rapidly, like a bird's swoop, as an infaʿala form from قَضَضْتُه; alternatively it derives from naqḍ, or is read ينقاض like an eye splitting lengthwise.
rows.anchor: يقال انقض إذا أسرع سقوطه من انقضاض الطائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أقامه may mean he dismantled and rebuilt the wall, propped it up by hand, or wiped it with his hand until it stood upright, which would be a miracle.
rows.anchor: وقيل : مسحه بيده فقام واستوى وكان ذلك من معجزاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because they were hungry and needy, Moses forgot his promise and suggests Khidr charge for the wall work so they could buy food and meet other needs.
rows.anchor: فلأجل تلك الضرورة نسي موسى ما قاله من قوله : { إن سألتك عن شىء بعدها فلا تصاحبنى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هذا فراق may refer to the prior condition that another question would cause separation, now fulfilled, or to the third objection as the cause of parting.
rows.anchor: أن موسى عليه السلام قد شرط أنه إن سأله بعد ذلك سؤالا آخر يحصل الفراق

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal cites grammarians who say البين means connection, as in لقد تقطع بينكم; thus this is a parting of the connection between the two, with the source added to a place phrase.
rows.anchor: حكى القفال عن بعض أهل العربية أن البين هو الوصل لقوله تعالى : { لقد تقطع بينكم } فكان المعنى هذا فراق بيننا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the expression as this is a separation that occurred between me and you; phrasing such as the liar between me and you means one of us.
rows.anchor: هكذا قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr promises to explain the wisdom behind the three incidents; تأويل derives from a matter's eventual outcome, so asking its interpretation asks where it ends up.
rows.anchor: وأصل التأويل راجع إلى قولهم آل الأمر إلى كذا أي صار إليه
